issue.title: Time-check canary times out in gear 2: asks Core on CPU with a 15 s limit (29 of ~31 checks in 24h)
issue.symptom: gaia_common/utils/heartbeat_time_check.py run_time_check() asks NANO_ENDPOINT (gaia-core localhost:8092) 'what time is it' with urlopen timeout=15. Since gear 2 became the resting gear (2qus), Core runs CPU GGUF on :8092 and the answer takes longer than 15 s, so the canary logs 'Heartbeat: ERROR — timed out' every ~15 min (29 since 2026-11-08 20:42 UTC). GAIA is fine; the canary is wrong. Fix: per-gear timeout (or ask the GPU tier), and don't count CPU slowness as death in /shared/heartbeat/time_check.json consumers (doctor).

investigation.format: issue_investigation actions: SEARCH / READ / PLACE + NOTE

gold_steps.why: a phrase or name from the issue, as it appears in code

gold_steps.note: The engine answers one request at a time; asleep, docs_maintenance holds Core on the CPU ~17 s per request and the canary queued behind it timed out about one check in fifteen while she was fine. HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS overrides.

regression_test.format: pytest functions added by the fix
